This year had its ups and downs, and knowing there were people here I could talk to, laugh with, or just sit quietly around made things feel lighter. Even on days I didn’t say much, it helped knowing you were there.

Thank you for the patience, the kindness, the chaos, and the moments that genuinely made me smile when I needed it most. You didn’t have to be that for me, but you were—and I don’t take that lightly.

I’m really grateful for every one of you. This place feels safe, warm, and real, and that’s because of the people in it. I’m glad we crossed paths, and I hope we keep sharing many more moments together 🩵 @everyone

[10/01/2026 11:31 am] adataztic
Once, there were four kingdoms that ruled side by side, even if they had different morals and traditions.
They were Valtheris, Aegoryn, Eirathis and Verdelune. Each kingdom has different types of Ambryss. Valtheris' are purple and black, while Aegoryn's are blue and red. Eirathis' are pink and orange, while Verdelune are green and yellow. Some represented royalty and knights, while others represented nobility, peasants, possibly more, by colour. 

When Zathaniel Thornheart was little, maybe 4 or 5 years old, Valtheris declared war. They swear by the fact that Ambryss could kill, could grant them power. They took that to heart. His father, a commander knight in Aegoryn, met with his mother, a farmer or gardener, decided to have his sister and then him. One night, him and his father decided to go to the forests to stargaze. His mother had asked his sister to pick up some fruits she had planted near their tent, where they had lived. She fell asleep soon after. Then, Valtheris knights started raid Aegoryn kingdom, in silence, when everyone had been asleep, at least that's what they've thought. His sister quickly heard the noise and decided to hide. Luckily, they didn't find out. His father realized too, as he saw them on the cliff they were sitting. He told Zathaniel to there, wait for him, while he goes a bit near to see more clearly. That's when after they left, his father went to their tent with Zathaniel to realise, they had killed his wife. He fell down in grief and tears, while little Zathaniel was confused. His sister had left, running, into the woods, thinking her brother and father had been missing. That's when she realized they were nowhere to be found. She decided to live in the woods instead, thinking her brother and father had been killed, alongside with her mother.

Meaning is not easily found, nor is it easily created. Finding it is the goal, the value that shapes a person and gives them meaning. The time spent living is valuable, and without this value, a person loses their most important motivation for living. Meaning is linked to hope, and if hope for meaning is lost, a person loses their reason for living and cannot continue. Even if they manage to continue, it will be a futile and meaningless continuation, like a hollow, desolate man, unfilled by anything.

Here, Shinji's character serves as an example of this painful reality. He lives to seek recognition from his father, and when he loses this hope, his features fade. Shinji fades, becoming an empty shell. To create meaning, we must not lose hope. We must feel that there is a light at the end of the tunnel, and even if we don't see it, simply believing that it is not clear allows us to continue and move forward.

[12/04/2026 7:39 pm] monoandmyfriend6 (pinned)
Dear server members and snoofies,

Please do not panic about the recent "hacking" rumors. Accounts do not just get hacked "by magic." In 99% of cases, one of two things happened:

Active Phishing: You clicked a link or downloaded something (maybe days or weeks ago – viruses can have an "incubation period" like a cold!).

Credential Stuffing: You used the same password on multiple sites. If a small website gets leaked, hackers try that password everywhere else (Instagram, Discord, Roblox).

Stay safe with these rules:

NO "Free Nitro/Robux" links. If it sounds too good to be true, it is a trap.

Unique Passwords: Use a different password for every single platform.

Do not use AI for passwords: Never ask ChatGPT or Gemini for passwords – they are logged on servers and are not truly random.

Manual entropy: If you do not trust password managers, write your passwords on physical paper in printed letters. Keep that paper safe (Money box/Hidden safe)!

Enable 2FA: Use an Authenticator App. It is the best shield we have.

Stay smart and do not let the panic-bugs bite!

{Reactions}

[23/06/2026 10:45 pm] 0_____________________________.0
Here's my take, past the condescending messages and fallacies: 

I always quote this personal anecdote; "Awareness of death is what gives life meaning"

I think it's contradictory in every perspective whether death is Good or bad. I'm not here to discuss whether death is good or bad because in these contexts, good or bad is not defined. Judgement can only be extrapolated based on an individual's belief and/or assumption of perception of death itself. 

To question death itself is a mistake. It's a fact.  Inherently death serves no meaning other than to limit the existence of human individuals. However you try to interpret that is beyond the scope of the argument unless you want to hold two arguments at once; this has been a ongoing debate of theologists and philosophers for thousands of years till now. 


If you want my take on the arguments you yourselves make, then I'd have to take Jad's side, not because he's correct, but because he speaks within the scope of the argument he presents himself. He is simply "more correct" in this area. 

If we're talking about the nature of the arguments for and against death, then the arguments become unfalsifiable in the eyes of the beholder. Rather than discussion about death, a more meaningful debate would be to discuss the meaning of life. 

Hope this helps.
